overview: Scoping review following JBI guidance and reported with PRISMA-ScR, charting technicians' roles in medication reconciliation at admission, transfer and discharge, from October 2026 to March 2027.
population: Reports (journal articles, theses, programme descriptions, regulatory and professional documents) describing pharmacy technicians taking medication histories or reconciling medications at a care transition, from 2000, in English.
exposure: Technician involvement in reconciliation tasks: history taking, list comparison, discrepancy documentation, referral and resolution.
procedures: The library builds searches in three bibliographic databases and professional organisation websites; titles and abstracts are screened by two reviewers if the resident is released, otherwise by one reviewer with a second checking a 20 percent sample. A charting form, tested on the seven retrieved records, records setting, transition, tasks, training, supervision model, accuracy measure and reference standard, outcome definitions, jurisdiction and date of scope statements, and rural or weekend coverage.

outcomes.name: Technician tasks by transition
outcomes.measure: Charted list of reconciliation tasks performed by technicians at admission, transfer and discharge
outcomes.why: The committee's decision is about which tasks to extend.

outcomes.name: Training and supervision models
outcomes.measure: Charted training length, competency assessment and supervision model
outcomes.why: Safety depends on supervision as much as on the task.

outcomes.name: Reported outcomes and their definitions
outcomes.measure: Charted outcomes (discrepancies, potential harm, readmission, workload, patient-reported) with each definition

outcomes.name: Screening agreement
outcomes.measure: Kappa between reviewers on the screened sample
outcomes.why: Shows how reliable screening was with the reviewer arrangement actually used.

outcomes.name: Reports excluded for language
outcomes.measure: Count of otherwise eligible reports excluded because no English version exists
outcomes.why: No translation budget; the bias is reported.

feasibility: About 80 hours of pharmacist time from October to March at four hours a week; dual screening depends on the resident's release.
biasMitigation: Charting form tested on the seven retrieved records before full screening
Jurisdiction and date recorded for every scope statement
Grey literature searched on professional organisation websites
Reports excluded for language counted and listed

biasFlags.label: Single-reviewer screening
biasFlags.note: If the resident is not released, a 20 percent verification sample limits missed reports.

biasFlags.label: Language restriction
biasFlags.note: No translation budget; excluded reports are counted.

biasFlags.label: Publication bias toward successful programmes
biasFlags.note: Grey literature and regulatory sources partly offset it.

flags: Charting items limited to the committee's five questions
parsimony.simplestPath: One PCC question, one charting form, descriptive synthesis.

theoreticalFramework: JBI scoping review method; no additional framework.
summary: JBI scoping review with one primary charted concept, two secondary, and two process measures that expose the reviewer and language limits.
